Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 70, verses 32–39:

His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying:

﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant.﴾ ﴿And those who stand firm in their testimonies.﴾ ﴿And those who guard their prayers.﴾ ﴿These will be in gardens, honoured.﴾ ﴿So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, rushing toward you,﴾ ﴿from the right and from the left, in groups?﴾ ﴿Does every one of them aspire to enter a Garden of bliss?﴾ ﴿No! Indeed, We created them from what they know.﴾

"Al-amanat" (الأمانات, trusts) is the plural of amanah (أمانة, trust). It is used in the plural because trusts are varied, in terms of wealth, secrets, and what lies between the servant and his Lord concerning what He has commanded and forbidden. Al-Hasan said: "The whole of religion is a trust." Ibn Kathir alone among the seven (the seven canonical readers) read لأمانتهم (li-amanatihim) in the singular. "Al-'ahd" (العهد, covenant) is everything a person binds himself to, whether by word, deed, or affection. When these things are upon the path of righteousness, it is a covenant that must be observed and preserved. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Keeping the covenant well is part of faith." "Ra'un" (راعون) is the plural of ra'in (راع), meaning one who guards or preserves.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who stand firm in their testimonies﴾ means, according to a group of the exegetes, that they preserve what they testify to, are certain of it, and uphold its meanings so that they fall short in nothing concerning it. This is a description drawn from the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying, peace be upon him: "Bear witness to what is like the sun." Others said its meaning is: those who, when they hold testimony and see a truth being effaced, or a sanctity of God being violated, rise to give their testimony. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Their testimony in this verse is that Allah, alone, has no partner." It is also reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The best of witnesses is the one who brings his testimony before he is asked for it." People differed about the meaning of this hadith according to the two meanings we have mentioned in the verse. One is that he has the two (testimony and its content) firmly memorised, so he brings it forth and does not need to be asked about any part of it or to be contradicted. The second is that he sees a truth being acted against while he holds testimony that can revive that truth. It is also reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There will come a people who will be accused of treachery and not be trusted, who will bear witness without being asked to, and among whom corpulence will appear." People differed about the meaning of this hadith. Some said: they are believers who put themselves forward and eagerly seek to have their names entered into people's documents, and set snares for that through appearance and bearing, while they are not upright in themselves, so they deceive and harm by this means.

The Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

This refers to the initiation of testimony, not its delivery. His peace and blessings be upon him, saying "and they are not asked to testify" means that they are not fit for that role.

Others among the scholars said: they are false witnesses, who give testimony when the one against whom it is given did not call them to it, nor did the other party.

Hafs, from 'Asim, read بِشَهاداتِهِمْ (bi-shahadatihim, in the plural), and this is the reading of 'Abd al-Rahman. The rest read بِشَهادَتِهِمْ (bi-shahadatihim, in the singular), which is the generic noun. "Al-muhafazah 'ala al-salah" (المحافظة على الصلاة, guarding the prayer) means performing it at its appointed times, with its conditions for validity and completeness. Ibn Jurayj said: voluntary prayer is included in this verse. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, rushing toward you﴾, and the rest of the verse, was revealed because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sometimes pray near the Ka'bah and recite the Qur'an. Many of the disbelievers would rise from their gatherings, hastening towards him to listen to his recitation, and some of them would say to one another: "A poet," "a soothsayer," "a fabricator," and other such things. "Qibalaka" (قِبَلَكَ) means: in front of you, in your direction. "Al-muhti'" (المهطع) is one who walks swiftly towards something on which he has fixed his gaze. Ibn Zayd said: he does not blink.

"'Izin" (عزين) is the plural of 'izzah (عزة). Some grammarians said its original form is 'izwah, and others among them said its original form is 'izhah, and it was pluralised with the waw and nun as a substitute for what was elided from it, like sanah (year) and sununa (years). The meaning of 'izzah is a small group, as though they were saying: three by three, and four by four. From this is the saying of al-Ra'i (the poet):

O Caliph of the Merciful, indeed my tribe,
their chiefs have come to you in scattered groups.

Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) went out to his companions while they were in scattered circles, and said: 'What is the matter with me that I see you in groups?'" His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Does every one of them aspire to enter a Garden of bliss?﴾ was revealed because some of the disbelievers said: "If there is indeed an Afterlife and a Garden, then we are its people and it is ours, because Allah has not bestowed upon us in this world wealth, sons and other things except out of His pleasure with us."

The Seven, al-Hasan, and the majority read يُدْخَلَ (yudkhala, passive, with damma on the ya' and fatha on the kha'). Al-Mufaddal from 'Asim, Ibn Ya'mur, Abu Raja' and Talhah read يَدْخُلَ (yadkhula, active, with fatha on the ya' and damma on the kha'), building the verb for the subject. His saying, the Exalted: "Kalla" (كلا, No!) is a rejection of their claim and their aspiration, meaning: the matter is not as they suppose.

Then the Exalted informed of their creation from a foul drop, and He referred in the expression to what people know about it. That is: whoever is created from that, the act of creating him does not by itself grant him the Garden; rather it is through righteous deeds, if he has them. Qatadah said in its explanation: "You were only created from filth, son of Adam, so fear Allah, the Exalted." Anas said: "When Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, addressed us, he would mention the foulness of the son of Adam, his passage through the path of urine twice, and his being a drop in the womb, then a clot, then a lump, until he comes out and is soiled with his impurities as an infant. Abu Bakr would not stop until one of us was disgusted with himself."
